changed_in.5.3: Reading a string as a number accepts both a dot and the character the current locale names, so a numeral written with a dot still reads as one after the numeric category has been moved. Earlier versions hand such text straight to the C library, which takes only the character the locale names: under a locale that uses a comma, `tonumber("3.5")` answers `nil` there and `3.5` here, while `tonumber("3,5")` answers `3.5` on both. What this call does, what it accepts and what it answers with are unchanged, and so is the way a number is written back out.
